scene_summary: A textured lavender-blue painted field holds a dense iris clump on the left and a smaller, lighter clump on the right. Violet and yellow blossoms punctuate overlapping green leaves. One conspicuous forest-green blade arches from the left clump across the upper middle, ending in a fine downward hook. This planned anchor is visible, but the many surrounding leaves and all-over brushwork make the composition busier than a minimal expressionist plate.
usable_surfaces: Long arching forest-green iris blade with a broken teal edge

detected_objects.label: Long hooked forest-green iris blade with broken teal brushstroke edge
detected_objects.visual_evidence: A continuous dark-green arch rises diagonally from the upper-right edge of the dense left foliage, crosses the pale lavender-blue field, and tapers into a downward-pointing tip. Its upper rim and hooked end have visibly interrupted teal strokes. The polygon follows this blade alone, excluding the neighboring upright leaves and the smaller curved leaves below. Its lower attachment merges into overlapping foliage and is less sharply distinguishable than the exposed arch.

complexity_assessment.rationale: The left iris mass, exposed hooked blade, and smaller right iris mass organize the image around a broad lavender-blue field. The planned blade remains recognizable, but dense overlapping foliage and persistent background brushwork prevent a genuinely minimal reading. Only the single planned source-bearing blade is mapped; the surrounding flowers and leaves remain subordinate context.
